## Burnstate features

### Your AI limits, in the menu bar

Meet Ember, a tiny flame that watches your coding tools. Its face tells you if an agent is working, an agent needs you, or a limit is running hot. You can also show the percent for any one limit right next to it.

### Limits paced against the clock

Every limit gets a bar with a clock tick that shows how far through its window you are. Burning too fast? A forecast tells you when you'll run out, like "runs out 15:04, 38m before reset". Providers are sorted, so the one that needs you is on top.

It follows your agent sessions live and lets you answer their permission prompts from a small card. When it's time to step away, it reminds you to take a break. No account, no analytics, and your usage stays on your Mac. [...] ### All your tools in one place

Track Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Vercel AI Gateway, and Setapp AI. If a tool is already signed in on your Mac, Burnstate uses that login. If not, sign in with a one-time code or paste an API key. It never touches a tool's own login, so it can't sign you out of anything.

### Live Claude Code sessions

The Sessions tab lists every Claude Code session on your Mac, from any terminal or editor. Open one to see its tokens, cost, models, and last prompt. You can also copy a resume command or archive old sessions.

### Permission prompts on a card

When Claude Code wants to run a command or asks you something, a card pops up in the corner of your screen. Allow, deny, or answer right there. No more hunting for the right terminal window.

Only tools installed on your Mac get a card. A tool that's signed out stays visible and tells you what to do.

## Choose what the menu bar shows

Four menu bar setups: one Claude Code limit, Claude Code's session and weekly limits with tiny labels, four tools side by side, and Codex's weekly limit with three banked resets.

Show any tool and any limit it reports. A single limit shows just its number, several get tiny labels, and `↻3` counts the resets you have banked. Switch between what's left and what's used right in the panel.

AI Usage settings in the menu bar panel: a switch to track each tool, a switch to show it in the menu bar, and checkboxes for its limits, followed by number, refresh, and startup options. [...] Track every tool you use and choose exactly what reaches the menu bar. Usage refreshes every 1, 5, 15, 30, or 60 minutes, and the refresh button works any time.

 How the menu bar decides what to show

 Weekly is selected for Claude Code and Codex at first, and Left is the default number mode.
 When a selected limit is missing, such as Claude's session window on accounts that have none, the tool's default limit is shown instead.
 The panel lists when each banked reset expires and turns the next one orange in its final 24 hours.
 Percentages are shown exactly as the provider reports them. Only the bars are clamped to `0...100`, and a remaining percentage never goes below zero.

## Privacy [...] Coding agents stop mid-task when a limit runs out. AI Usage keeps the numbers one glance away: what's left of every session and weekly limit, when each one resets, and how many banked resets you can still spend. It reuses the logins your tools already have, so there is nothing to set up.

 Nothing to set up. No account, API key, or password. If you're signed in to a tool, AI Usage can read its limits.
 Private. It talks only to each provider's own usage endpoint. No analytics, no servers of ours, no usage history.
 Light. Measured at 0.0% CPU between refreshes. The panel is released as soon as it closes.
 Native. SwiftUI and Liquid Glass in light and dark, with signed automatic updates.
